sections.h2: Indian refiners' fuel margin fell to $4–6/bbl from $10–12/bbl

chart.title: Indian OMC refining margin fell by roughly half in one year
chart.source: CareEdge tracking of the sector, as cited in the post.

sections.means: Refining margin per barrel has fallen far enough to give refiners a reason to shift output toward LPG and petrochemicals.
sections.todo: Track the next quarters of margin data before treating the fall as lasting, since the post says these margins are cyclical.

sections.h2: Imports absorbed LPG demand growth while domestic output barely moved

chart.title: LPG import dependency rose every year, from 48.7% to 60.7%
chart.sub: Imports as a share of LPG consumption, %.
chart.source: PPAC Ready Reckoner, Table 7.1 "LPG marketing at a glance".

sections.means: Domestic LPG production stayed flat while imports met nearly all of the rise in consumption.
sections.todo: Treat the growing import share as a gap that domestic LPG output from a refinery could fill.

sections.h2: Cheaper propane and butane and state support narrowed the LPG supply gap

chart.title: LPG under-recovery narrowed from ₹98.6 to ₹33 per cylinder
chart.sub: Gap between supply cost and recovery from consumers, ₹ per cylinder.

sections.means: Lower propane and butane prices and government compensation both moved in LPG's favour as its fuel margin was falling.
sections.todo: Check whether the narrower gap holds once the monthly government compensation stops.

sections.h2: The polymer spread over naphtha widened sharply in the latest window

chart.title: LDPE-naphtha spread widened from $354 to $566 a tonne
chart.sub: Polymer margin over feedstock cost, $/tonne, October to March.

sections.means: Over the latest six-month window the polymer side of the barrel was the steadier and wider-margin route.
sections.todo: Expect petrochemical spreads to be cyclical and re-check them before committing capital.
